Pause for approval

You will make the refund agent ask a person before it moves money. The run ends with a signed request that you can store as JSON, and any process with the key can resume it. You need this when a write must not run unattended.

Write the gate

Section titled “Write the gate”

The gate is an interceptor. It asks a person before any refund_create call and allows everything else:

Store the pause

Section titled “Store the pause”

Start the run with a signer, which signs each request. The default signer holds a random key that lives only in its own process, so another process rejects its signatures. Pass hmacSigner() over a key ring you store, so any process that holds the key can verify the request.

When the result’s stop reason is awaiting_approval, save result.context with your own store. It holds the pending requests and the input each one signs. Show the person that input, not the model’s arguments, because the gate or a repair step may have changed them.

Resume with the person’s answer

Section titled “Resume with the person’s answer”

Pass the stored context and one resolution for each request to continueRun(). This function resumes the refund run:

The SDK checks each resolution against its signature before the call runs. A resolution that fails its check runs nothing, and the call asks again.
